claims.text: All 10 controls behave exactly as designed against BOTH the pre-repair and post-repair gate — harness exit 0, zero deviations. Six behaviours changed, every one in the intended direction: M4 0->1, M5 1->0, M6 1->2, M7 1->0, M8 0->2, M9 0->2.

DEFECT-1 CLOSED — deleting the boss_stability row from the registry (M4) previously left the gate green at exit 0. The repaired gate now requires every governed counter to be PRESENT and exits 1 with "NOT IN REGISTRY — governed counter went missing". Absence is no longer indistinguishable from denial.

DEFECT-2 CLOSED — the A2-writable column is now located BY HEADER NAME, not by position. Inserting a benign third column (M5) previously caused a false alarm at exit 1 while making all five deny assertions pass vacuously; it now correctly exits 0 with every assertion still evaluated against the real verdict cell.

DEFECT-3 CLOSED — the exit-code collision is gone. The doc path is now __file__-relative: measured exit 0 from all five working directories that previously produced exit 1 with 799 bytes of FileNotFoundError. A missing registry (M6) now exits 2 ("could not evaluate"), which no longer collides with exit 1 ("gate violated").

NEW DEFECT FOUND AND CLOSED — DEFECT-4. Replacing the boss_stability verdict cell with unparseable text (M8: "TBD") made the ORIGINAL gate exit 0. A cell it could not read was silently treated as "denied", so a registry that no longer states an authority verdict still reported ALL GATE CONDITIONS MET. The repaired gate exits 2. This defect was not in my Task A report; it was found by extending the control set during the repair.

NEW DEFECT FOUND AND CLOSED — DEFECT-5. Renaming the "**A2-writable via E11**" column header away (M9) made the ORIGINAL gate exit 0. The write-scope column IS the authority repair; deleting it is a document regression that the gate reported as fully compliant. The repaired gate exits 2 and names the missing column.

The repaired gate passes the canonical registry in place: exit 0, 0 bytes stderr, 6 counters parsed from §4.1, all 7 cases PASS. Registry document is byte-identical after the repair (747ad8742419ead63b5435e0dee0d60d717849124e0e17a6332bf215e05aec5b) — the repair touched only the test.

SELF-REPORTED, REPRODUCED — my first repair shipped the same defect class it was fixing. The verdict parser used a bare substring test, and "NO" occurs inside "CANON", which appears in the boss_release_delay justification text. The cell parsed as both YES and NO and the gate exited 2 on the HONEST registry. Caught by the M0 unmutated control, then fixed to match the document's bold **YES**/**NO** marker via regex. The broken form is reconstructed and its failure captured rather than described.

The SCOPE limit from Task A is preserved verbatim in the repaired file's docstring: this checks the REGISTRY DOCUMENT, not product code; there is still no E11 admission path in the UE tree; the enforcement requirement at RX_SKILL_ENUMS_V1.md:261-266 remains UNMET IN CODE. A stronger gate over a document is still a gate over a document, and the file now says so at the top.

python3 test_e11_authority_gate.py   # my first repair, substring parser

decisions_requested: The repaired gate adds exit code 2 ("could not evaluate") alongside 0 and 1. Any CI wrapper that treats non-zero as breach will now report a harness fault as a breach — better than the old collision, but wrappers should branch on 1 vs 2. Confirm no existing runner depends on the old two-value contract.
risks: The gate is stronger but still checks a DOCUMENT. DEFECT-1..5 were all failures to read the registry honestly; none of them, fixed, brings an E11 validator into existence. A.5 and the missing admission path are unchanged by this work.

PROCESS DEFECT, REPEATED: I overwrote the failing repair_matrix.out with the passing rerun before preserving it — the same artifact-loss mistake I reported for N6 in Task B. I caught it this time and reconstructed the broken parser to capture its failure as evidence, but the correct habit is to write failing runs to a distinct filename FIRST. Two occurrences in one cycle makes this a habit defect, not a slip.

My first repair reproduced the exact defect class under repair (substring matching). That it was caught only by the unmutated M0 control is the argument for always carrying a canonical-fixture control alongside the negative ones.
next_action: Checklist A and B complete; A.5 OPEN by ruling. E11 gate defects 1-5 closed and verified. Awaiting next assignment or L4/L5 disposition on whether A closes on document evidence.
